subject: OrchidHealth demo: performance decision matrix & clarifying targets
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Devon Lee <devon.lee@orchidhealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T09:15:00Z
Subject: OrchidHealth — demo recap & quick performance clarifications

Hi Samira / Devon,

Thanks again for your time on the call — appreciated the detailed walkthrough of the use case and sample traffic. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can map acceptance criteria to a concrete test plan: 

1) Latency target: you mentioned 95th <= 350ms for conversational turns under streaming. Is that target for median 1-token latency (streaming chunks) or end-of-turn (full response)?
2) Concurrency: expected concurrent active users during peak = ~120; is that concurrent websocket connections or concurrent in-flight requests?
3) Throughput: during peak you said ~600 requests/minute sustained for ~10 minutes bursts — please confirm if spikes up to 1,200 RPM are possible during promo windows.
4) Streaming: you require token-level streaming with partial results and the option to cancel mid-response. Any constraints on max response length?

Next steps I propose: we map each item above to an acceptance criteria row (latency measure, percentile, traffic shape, model variant) and run a 1-hour soak on Dedicated trial capacity. If that sounds good I can share a mutual action plan (MAP) and an initial perf checklist for your SREs to review.

Attaching a short performance requirements summary and a draft MAP for your review. 

Thanks — I’ll loop Karthik and Monica to coordinate the trial slots once you confirm the traffic shapes.

— Ava
Ava Chen | Enterprise Sales (Performance)
Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0132

From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchidhealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Devon Lee <devon.lee@orchidhealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T13:02:00Z
Subject: Re: OrchidHealth — demo recap & quick performance clarifications

Hi Ava — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below: 

1) Latency: the 350ms target is for end-of-turn perceived latency (i.e., the user sees first readable tokens within ~350ms and final completion within 1.2s). 95th percentile is our SLA target.
2) Concurrency: 120 concurrent *active* users, where each 'active' user may have an open websocket and occasional in-flight requests (so treat as concurrent connections).
3) Throughput: sustained 600 RPM is typical during business hours; we can spike to 1,200 RPM for ~5–10 minutes during scheduled events. 
4) Streaming: must support token-level streaming and cancelation. Max response length for current MVP is ~1,000 tokens, though most responses are <300 tokens.

We’re also sensitive to cost — if quantized model variants can meet the end-to-end SLA we’d prefer those. Happy to review the MAP and schedule the soak. Can you propose two 1-hour windows next week?

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Automation
OrchidHealth
samira.khan@orchidhealth.com

Samira — perfect, that helps a ton. Two quick follow-ups so we can prepare the soak configuration and pick the right model family: 

• Which is more important if we need to trade off: strict 95th end-of-turn latency vs cost? (they indicated cost sensitivity; please rank).
• For streaming cancelation semantics: do you expect the client to call a cancel endpoint mid-response, or will the UX close the websocket? Either is fine but we need to know to enable early-kv-cache-release heuristics.

- Tues 2026-08-11 10:00–11:00

I’m looping Karthik to confirm model/quantization recommendations and Monica for project coordination (MAP).

Folks — internal plan based on Samira's replies: 

1) Acceptance matrix (attached): map percentile => measurement API call => traffic pattern. We’ll test both quantized (+2–3% quality risk) and FP16 variants.
2) Soak window: confirm Tue 2026-08-11 10:00–11:00 (preferred) — Monica will book Dedicated trial GPU slots and share credentials with Orchid SREs.
3) Test composition: 20-minute ramp to 600 RPM sustained, 5x 2-minute spikes to 1,200 RPM during the hour, streaming token-by-token with cancel calls at 50% of sessions. Measure 50/95/99 latency on token-first and end-of-turn.
4) Decision criteria: pass if 95th end-of-turn <= 350ms AND P99 token-first < 800ms, with acceptable memory/KV stability. If quantized variant passes we recommend that first for cost reasons; fallback to FP16 for strict quality.

Attachments included in this thread: orchid_mvp_map.xlsx (MAP with owners & dates), orchid_perf_req_summary.pdf (measurement summary). HubSpot deal ORCH-2457 has been updated with the acceptance criteria.

Ava — Monica will need the HubSpot link and your sales collateral for the kickoff. I’ll schedule the internal perf run on our staging cluster next week to validate harness scripts.

Thanks — Karthik
